text:
By Mike Brant ,
15 hours ago Canva (Townsquare Illustration) Groundhog Day is now in the rearview mirror, and I think I can speak for most New Jerseyans when I say this. All rodents that predicted six more weeks of this ridiculously cold winter are not on a very good list with us right now.
But that aside, Feb. 2 isn‚Äôt the date that should matter to us in New Jersey. It‚Äôs the days that come right afterward. Feb. 4, in particular, is a glorious day we should be celebrating.

Feb. 3 marks the half way point of winter, and Feb. 4 marks that official point that we‚Äôre on the backside of the month.
Yup, we officially made it over the ‚ÄúWednesday‚Äù of winter. Or in other words, the hump day of the season. From here on out, it‚Äôs a mad rush to the finish line.
Photo by Jeff Swensen/Getty Images Why Groundhog Day is more depressing Here‚Äôs the problem with the annual Groundhog Day celebration. When we highlight we still have six long weeks of winter to go, it just sounds so depressing. Almost like we still have a really long stretch of miserable coldness.
On the flip side, knowing we‚Äôve crossed the half way point just seems more satisfying. Rather than focusing on the cold, let‚Äôs focus on the official countdown.
Photo by Shawn Dearn on Unsplash Overthinking, or a better perspective? I know, this may be overanalyzing it, but I don‚Äôt care. The fact still remains that this winter has been incredibly brutal, and we need something more to look forward to instead of hearing that we still have six more weeks of it.
Don‚Äôt tell us we have six more weeks to go. Tell us we‚Äôre now over the hump and that we‚Äôre now in that home stretch getting to spring.
